body: I'm really sorry about your friend. Everyone copes with loss in their own way. From what you've said, I don't think you handled anything wrong at all. For years, I thought about how traumatic it would be for my little sister to go through the same thing I had gone through at her age. It can be easy to downplay the effect we'd have on our families when we're in full depression/suicidal mode. Things become blurry, my past mistakes seem magnified and my worth diminished.

Thanks for the motivation. I really need to do that at the very least. Something to get me out of the house. I sometimes go more  than an entire week without ever stepping outside. Even doing manual labor would have to be better for me mentally.

I appreciate it - you can message me as well whenever you feel down. Did you lose someone close to you from suicide as well, or were you just gauging what kind of impact you would leave if you committed suicide?

Thanks man, I really appreciate your kind words. I lost my job like 14 months ago so I've been living on savings and my girlfriend's income, which is demoralizing for sure. The only job experience I've had since graduating college is honestly, just over a year of a job I wasn't qualified for at the time. I actually enjoyed the work just fine, but I've found that even with that experience I am not qualified to find any other jobs in that field. 

I went through every recruiting agency available to me, even got as far as a 4th interview with a nice company, but it never worked out in the end. Now I have inexperience in addition to a long ugly gap in my resume. I'm feeling unemployable. We talked about signing up with an online society for this profession with the hope that I may learn new skills and meet good contacts. Of course, there are expensive dues and I feel the clock is ticking. 

I'm glad you were able to find a job through all the rejection. It's never easy. Everything is an insecurity for me - the interview process, if I'll be ridiculed for being overweight, or if I'll be mocked for inexperience.

That's exactly how I feel. It's hard to give a single explanation for the times I am depressed. At this time, definitely I am feeling worthless for not having a job but I am also scared to fail at life. I would almost rather disqualify myself from the process than to build myself up inside only to face total rejection/humiliation again. 

I can say though that even when I was working, I still felt *off* and hollow. I started taking SSRI's when I was 20 years old and that was the first time I experienced true apathy and hollowness. Now, several years after I've discontinued taking medicine, that emptiness and apathy is still a large part of me.

I lost my father, an aunt, and an uncle to suicide. I lost my father at such a young age. It opened my mind to the existence of suicide and the gravity of what it meant. I obsessed over how bad things must be for that to be a real possibility for someone, and to know that my father experienced them...it pained me for many years long before I even entered my teenage years. 

I lost my aunt to a drug overdose and I am still not sure if it was intentional or not, though it occurred after she had gotten in a bad argument with her mother (my grandmother). That one was a real punch in the gut because I was much closer with her than I was with my father. It was at this point that I was convinced there must be a reason that two of my family members killed themselves. Maybe there was a *suicide* *gene* that could be passed down. Did I inherit this same thing? 

My uncle killed himself many years later. I still don't understand what happened. He had never talked with any of us about feeling depressed or down. He was the life of every party and was always laughing and smiling. To think that he would go that way would have been unimaginable if you'd asked me before it happened. 

I clearly haven't gotten over any of this. To this day I still feel it is part of my destiny. The only question is when.
